reference: GNU coreutils env, invoked by the same scripts under system Bash. The runner validates the stated reference status and compares stdout bytes, stderr policy, and fixture trees against the candidate. Expected contract output for the metadata case is based on Bash type/help builtins and env_doc in the pinned source.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and registered help metadata
Clean environment printing, assignment values, duplicate assignment behavior, and NUL delimiters
GNU -S quoting and expansion of an exported variable
Relative -C execution, command argv0 override, and private fixture file effects
External child environment bytes and last-wins ordering, including -S and NUL output
Explicit/empty argv[0] versus modified relative PATH lookup
Caller cwd, exported and unexported variables and PATH preservation; child and chdir failure statuses
exclusions: Signal disposition and mask options are not exercised in this bounded suite.
Debug output and version text are omitted because this suite focuses on execution and environment behavior.
Metadata is a Bash contract, not GNU operation coverage. No host child commands are executed; all fixtures run only through the mandatory isolated worker.

cases.purpose: Check that Bash identifies env as a builtin and that help env exposes the documented env_doc description.
cases.script: [[ $(type -t env) == builtin ]]; [[ $(help env) == *'Print or modify the environment'* ]]; printf 'builtin; help documented\n'

cases.purpose: Verify -i prints only explicitly supplied assignments and preserves spaces and embedded equals signs in values.
Check GNU env's replacement semantics when the same variable is assigned more than once in a clean environment.
Compare raw NUL-delimited output for values containing spaces and equals signs.
Remove an exported caller variable, PATH, and Bash's per-command underscore marker while adding a value containing whitespace; compare the resulting environment listing with GNU env.
cases.script: export ENV_DROP=remove; env -u PATH -u ENV_DROP -u _ ENV_KEEP='two words'

cases.purpose: Check GNU -S quote handling, an escaped newline, and preservation of a quoted argument containing a space.
Check that -S expands a variable exported earlier in the same Bash process, matching GNU env's environment-based expansion.
Exercise relative mkdir, file creation, hard and symbolic links, copy, move, chmod, and removal inside the fixture, then verify -C runs pwd in that directory and compare all file effects.
cases.script: mkdir -p workdir; printf payload > workdir/source; touch workdir/marker; ln workdir/source workdir/hard; ln -s source workdir/symbolic; cp workdir/source workdir/copied; mv workdir/copied workdir/final; chmod 0640 workdir/final; rm workdir/marker; env -i -C workdir pwd

cases.purpose: Preserve the original GNU comparison: modified system PATH lookup and argv[0] override together. An explicit-path case isolates the override.
Isolate GNU argv[0] override with an explicit child shell path; command lookup is tested separately.
Check GNU env's usage-error status and nonempty diagnostic for -u without an operand.
Check the conventional 127 status and diagnostic when env cannot find a requested command in a clean environment.
Repeated assignments replace the first slot, retain interspersed variable order, and preserve exact NUL delimiters.
cases.script: env -i -0 A=first B=middle A=last C=end B=final

cases.purpose: Observe the raw exec environment in an external child, including interspersed duplicate assignments.
The -S assignment parser must also replace duplicate names.
Search the modified PATH relative to the child working directory and preserve long-form argv[0].
cases.script: mkdir -p child/bin; ln -s /bin/sh child/bin/probe; env -i -C child --argv0=child-name PATH=bin probe -c 'printf "<%s>|<%s>\n" "$0" "$PATH"'

cases.purpose: GNU accepts an explicitly empty argv[0] for an external child shell.
Check child duplicate values, clean/unset environment, -C, argv[0], and status 7; verify caller exported/unexported variables, PATH, and cwd survive success and failed chdir.
cases.script:
mkdir child; export ENV_KEEP=caller ENV_DROP=remove; ENV_LOCAL=private; saved_path=$PATH; saved_pwd=$PWD; rc=0; env -i -C child -a child-name PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ENV_KEEP=first ENV_KEEP=last /bin/sh -c 'printf "<%s>|<%s>|<%s>|<%s>|<%s>
" "$0" "$ENV_KEEP" "${ENV_DROP-unset}" "${ENV_LOCAL-unset}" "${PWD##*/}"; exit 7' || rc=$?; printf 'child-status=%s
' "$rc"; [[ $rc == 7 ]]; [[ $ENV_KEEP == caller && $ENV_DROP == remove && $ENV_LOCAL == private && $PATH == "$saved_path" && $PWD == "$saved_pwd" ]]; env -u ENV_DROP -u ENV_LOCAL /bin/sh -c 'printf "<%s>|<%s>
" "$ENV_KEEP" "${ENV_DROP-unset}"'; rc=0; env -i -C absent /bin/sh -c 'exit 0' || rc=$?; printf 'chdir-status=%s
' "$rc"; [[ $rc == 125 ]]; [[ $ENV_KEEP == caller && $ENV_DROP == remove && $ENV_LOCAL == private && $PATH == "$saved_path" && $PWD == "$saved_pwd" ]]; printf 'caller-preserved
'; [[ $(declare -p ENV_KEEP) == 'declare -x ENV_KEEP="caller"' ]]; [[ $(declare -p ENV_LOCAL) == 'declare -- ENV_LOCAL="private"' ]]

cases.purpose: A relative non-executable private file found through modified PATH produces status 126 and a diagnostic.
